Maladaptive Strategies.value: constantly monitor own thoughts for signs of going crazy
Talking with others about the event or its aftermath
Being reminded of the event by others

Threat.value: I jump or startle at ordinary sounds that would not bother most people
Unusual silence makes me feel something dangerous is about to happen
I often react as if I am in danger even when nothing is actually wrong

Memory.value: My memories of the frightening event are mostly pictures or images.
When memories come to mind of what happened, I feel my body is in the same position as when the frightening event occurred.
Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory

Negative Appraisals.value: The world is a dangerous place
I have to be on guard all the time
I have to be especially careful because you never know what can happen next

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Physical Vulnerability: My body has been permanently damaged by what happened
issues.explanation: The appraisal of permanent bodily damage is hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile and trauma context. The other selected items consistently reflect ongoing external danger and hyperarousal (world dangerous, on guard, startle, false alarms, threat in silence) plus intrusive sensory memory, but there are no corroborating memory, threat, or strategy items indicating injury-focused trauma consequences, pain, disability, or body-related threat. For a refugee trauma profile, this isolated somatic-damage belief is not impossible, but in this item set it stands out as clinically incoherent with the dominant formulation of danger-based threat and avoidance.

vignette: Alessandro's eyes scan the crowded courtroom, his mind racing with the weight of his clients' stories. As a public defender, he has heard countless tales of trauma and hardship, but none resonate more deeply than his own. At 21, Alessandro is still grappling with the memories of his family's harrowing escape from war-torn Europe. It started on a chaotic night, as they fled their home amidst the sound of gunfire and screams. The visual memories of that evening remain etched in his mind like snapshots: the flash of a neighbor's terrified face, the shattered glass of their living room window, the eerie glow of flames engulfing their street. Even now, Alessandro can feel his body tense into the same crouched position he assumed as they huddled together, waiting for dawn to break. In the months that followed, Alessandro began to notice a creeping sense of unease. Ordinary sounds – a car backfiring, a door slamming shut – would startle him, leaving his heart racing and his senses on high alert. He found himself constantly scanning his surroundings, as if searching for potential threats lurking in every shadow. The silence was just as unsettling; an unusual stillness seemed to portend danger, making him jump at the slightest creak or rustle. Alessandro tried to talk about these feelings with his girlfriend, Rachel, but the words stuck in his throat. He couldn't shake the fear that she would think he was going crazy, that the memories and emotions swirling inside him were a sign of weakness. So he kept them locked away, hidden behind a mask of calm competence. As a result, Alessandro's relationships began to suffer. Rachel sensed his growing distance and tried to bridge the gap, but he pushed her away, unsure how to articulate the turmoil brewing within. His work as a public defender also took a toll; he found himself becoming increasingly hypervigilant in court, as if every case was a potential threat to his own safety. At times, Alessandro would feel the full emotional intensity of that night wash over him without any clear image or memory. It was as if his body remembered the terror even when his mind didn't. He began to believe that the world was a fundamentally treacherous place, and that he needed to be constantly on guard to avoid its dangers. As the months turned into years, Alessandro's avoidance behaviors became more entrenched. He stopped attending social gatherings or public events, fearing the noise and chaos would trigger another episode of startle response or false alarm. His relationships with colleagues and friends began to fray, as he grew increasingly withdrawn and isolated. It wasn't until Rachel confronted him about his growing distance that Alessandro realized he needed help. She gently pointed out the changes in his behavior, the way he flinched at every sudden noise, and the haunted look in his eyes when he thought no one was watching. For the first time, Alessandro felt a glimmer of hope – maybe he didn't have to live like this forever. As he sat in the therapist's office, Alessandro steeled himself for the conversation ahead. He knew it wouldn't be easy to confront the memories and emotions he had kept locked away for so long. But with Rachel by his side, he felt a sense of determination wash over him – he was ready to face whatever lay ahead, no matter how daunting it seemed.
